items.stem: The Every Student Succeeds Act, signed in December 2015, returned one major responsibility to the states that No Child Left Behind had held at the federal level. What was it?
items.stemEs: La Ley Todo Estudiante Triunfa, firmada en diciembre de 2015, devolvió a los estados una responsabilidad importante que la ley No Child Left Behind había mantenido en el nivel federal. ¿Cuál fue?

choices.text: Designing the accountability system — the goals, the measures beside test scores, and what happens to a school that falls short
choices.textEs: El diseño del sistema de rendición de cuentas: las metas, las medidas además de los resultados de las pruebas y lo que ocurre con una escuela que no cumple

choices.text: Deciding whether to test students in reading and mathematics at all
choices.textEs: Decidir si evaluar o no a los estudiantes en lectura y matemáticas
choices.explanation: Annual testing survived the change. Grades three through eight and once in high school, in both subjects, with results reported by student group — the newer law kept all of that and changed what is done with the results.
choices.misconception: treats a partial devolution of authority as the removal of the testing requirement itself

choices.text: Setting the academic content standards in each subject, which the earlier law had prescribed nationally for every state that took the funds
choices.textEs: La fijación de los estándares de contenido académico de cada materia, que la ley anterior había prescrito a nivel nacional para todos los estados que aceptaban los fondos
choices.explanation: Standards were never federal to give back. States wrote their own under the earlier law as well, which is why a proficient score meant different things in different states; what the newer law added was an explicit bar on the Secretary requiring any particular set.
choices.misconception: returns an authority to the states that the federal government never held

choices.text: Funding, which moved entirely onto state budgets when the newer law took effect
choices.textEs: La financiación, que pasó por completo a los presupuestos estatales cuando entró en vigor la ley más reciente
choices.explanation: Federal money continued — this is a reauthorisation of the same 1965 statute that carries Title I aid for schools serving low-income students, and that aid went on flowing. What moved was authority over accountability, not the appropriation.
choices.misconception: reads a transfer of decision-making authority as a transfer of the funding itself

items.dokRationale: Recall of what one statute moved and to whom. The student retrieves a provision; no reasoning about a court's two different holdings in a single case is involved. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that reasoning.
items.explanation: The newer law kept the measuring and gave back the judging. States still test annually in reading and mathematics and still report results by student group, but each state now writes its own plan for what counts as success, which indicators to use beside test scores, and what happens to a school that falls short — and the Secretary of Education is barred from requiring any particular set of standards.
items.explanationEs: La ley más reciente conservó la medición y devolvió el criterio. Los estados siguen evaluando cada año en lectura y matemáticas y siguen informando los resultados por grupo de estudiantes, pero ahora cada estado redacta su propio plan sobre qué cuenta como éxito, qué indicadores usar además de los resultados de las pruebas y qué ocurre con una escuela que no cumple; y al secretario de Educación se le prohíbe exigir cualquier conjunto concreto de estándares.

items.stem: In National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius (2012) the Supreme Court ruled on two parts of the Affordable Care Act and reached a different result on each. What were the two results?
items.stemEs: En National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius (2012), la Corte Suprema resolvió sobre dos partes de la Ley de Cuidado de Salud Asequible y llegó a un resultado distinto en cada una. ¿Cuáles fueron los dos resultados?

choices.text: It struck down the requirement to carry insurance and left the rest of the act standing
choices.textEs: Anuló la exigencia de tener seguro y dejó en pie el resto de la ley
choices.explanation: The requirement was upheld in this case, by five votes to four. What removed its force came later and from Congress rather than the Court: the 2017 tax law set the payment for not complying at zero.
choices.misconception: inverts the holding on the insurance requirement

choices.text: It upheld the insurance requirement under the Commerce Clause and upheld the Medicaid expansion exactly as Congress had written it
choices.textEs: Confirmó la exigencia de seguro en virtud de la Cláusula de Comercio y confirmó la ampliación de Medicaid exactamente como la había redactado el Congreso
choices.explanation: Both halves are the near miss. The commerce argument was the government's leading one and the controlling opinion rejected it, holding that the clause does not reach a decision not to buy something; and the expansion was not upheld as written.
choices.misconception: credits the holding to the clause the controlling opinion expressly declined to use

choices.text: It upheld the insurance requirement as an exercise of the taxing power, and made the Medicaid expansion optional for the states
choices.textEs: Confirmó la exigencia de seguro como ejercicio del poder tributario y convirtió la ampliación de Medicaid en opcional para los estados

choices.text: It struck down the subsidies available to people who bought coverage through the federally operated exchanges
choices.textEs: Anuló los subsidios disponibles para quienes compraban cobertura a través de los mercados operados por el gobierno federal
choices.explanation: Those subsidies were challenged and were UPHELD, in a different case three years later. Two separate decisions on one statute are easily merged, and this was the second of them.
choices.misconception: merges the 2012 decision with the separate 2015 decision on the exchange subsidies

items.dokRationale: A single case produced two holdings on two different provisions, and the student must hold both at once and get each the right way round. Recalling that the Court upheld the act is the DOK 1 version of this content, and it is also incomplete.
items.explanation: The Chief Justice's controlling opinion did two things at once. It sustained the requirement to carry insurance, not under the power to regulate commerce — which it expressly declined to stretch that far — but as a tax, because the only consequence of not complying was a payment collected with a tax return. And it held that cutting off a state's existing Medicaid funds for declining the expansion was unconstitutionally coercive, which left each state free to choose, and is why coverage differs by state to this day.
items.explanationEs: La opinión determinante del presidente de la Corte hizo dos cosas a la vez. Mantuvo la exigencia de tener seguro, no en virtud del poder de regular el comercio — que expresamente se negó a extender tanto — sino como un impuesto, porque la única consecuencia de no cumplir era un pago recaudado con la declaración de impuestos. Y resolvió que retirar a un estado los fondos de Medicaid que ya recibía por rechazar la ampliación era inconstitucionalmente coercitivo, lo que dejó a cada estado libre de elegir, y por eso la cobertura difiere entre estados hasta hoy.

items.stem: American combat forces left Iraq in December 2011 and American forces returned to the country in August 2014, during Barack Obama’s second term. What accounts for that reversal of the American presence in the Middle East?
items.stemEs: Las fuerzas de combate estadounidenses salieron de Irak en diciembre de 2011 y las fuerzas estadounidenses regresaron al país en agosto de 2014, durante el segundo mandato de Barack Obama. ¿Qué explica esa reversión de la presencia estadounidense en el Oriente Medio?

choices.text: Osama bin Laden's death in May 2011 had left the insurgency leaderless, so American forces were needed to restore order
choices.textEs: La muerte de Osama bin Laden en mayo de 2011 había dejado a la insurgencia sin liderazgo, de modo que se necesitaban fuerzas estadounidenses para restablecer el orden
choices.explanation: The death is real and its date is right. The organisation that took Mosul was not leaderless and was not weakened by it — it had broken with al-Qaeda in 2014 and grew stronger through the Syrian war, which is the opposite of the sequence this describes.
choices.misconception: treats two events three years apart as cause and effect because one preceded the other

choices.text: The Islamic State had taken Mosul and much of northern and western Iraq, and the Iraqi government asked for assistance
choices.textEs: El Estado Islámico había tomado Mosul y gran parte del norte y el oeste de Irak, y el gobierno iraquí pidió ayuda

choices.text: The nuclear agreement reached with Iran required an American military presence in the region to verify its terms
choices.textEs: El acuerdo nuclear alcanzado con Irán exigía una presencia militar estadounidense en la región para verificar sus términos
choices.explanation: The agreement is real and was concluded in July 2015, eleven months after the return in the question. Its inspections were carried out by the International Atomic Energy Agency and it required no deployment of any kind.
choices.misconception: cites an agreement signed after the event it is said to have caused

choices.text: The drawdown of American forces in Afghanistan had freed troops who were then redirected to Iraq
choices.textEs: La reducción de las fuerzas estadounidenses en Afganistán había liberado tropas que luego se redirigieron a Irak
choices.explanation: The drawdown was real and running through these years, so forces were indeed becoming available. Availability is not a reason to go: the question asks what made a return necessary, and a surplus of troops does not answer it.
choices.misconception: offers what made a deployment possible as the reason it was ordered

items.dokRationale: The student must connect a reversal of policy to the change on the ground that produced it, and reject three real events of the same administration that did not cause it. Recalling either date is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: The Islamic State took Mosul in June 2014 and held a broad stretch of northern and western Iraq within weeks, and the Iraqi government asked for help. American air operations began in August and advisers followed, under the argument that the 2001 and 2002 authorisations still applied — so an administration that had run on ending the war returned to it because the state it had left behind could not hold the ground.
items.explanationEs: El Estado Islámico tomó Mosul en junio de 2014 y en pocas semanas controlaba una amplia franja del norte y el oeste de Irak, y el gobierno iraquí pidió ayuda. Las operaciones aéreas estadounidenses comenzaron en agosto y luego llegaron asesores, con el argumento de que las autorizaciones de 2001 y 2002 seguían vigentes: una administración que se había presentado a las elecciones prometiendo terminar la guerra volvió a ella porque el Estado que había dejado atrás no podía sostener el territorio.
